AuditLogRead.description:
Read shape for an ``audit_log`` row.

Populated by ``record_change()`` on every CRUD touching a
resource. ``before`` / ``after`` are JSON snapshots — operators
use the diff to see exactly what changed.

``ts`` is naive UTC at rest (audit #121, v1.3.4); the Pydantic
serializer emits a Z-suffixed ISO so the UI can convert to the
operator's local time unambiguously.

get.description:
Returns every config table (inputs, variables, templates, channels, routes, rules, schedules, settings) as a portable YAML document. Identifiers across sections use NAMES, not auto-generated ids — safe to apply on a different deployment.

Set `?mask_secrets=true` to rewrite literal-looking secrets (bot_token, password, api_key fields) as `env:UNKNOWN_*` placeholders so the YAML is shareable.

post.description:
POST a YAML body with `?apply=true` to commit. Without `apply=true`, runs as a dry-run (same response shape as /validate). On apply: writes happen in a single transaction; any error rolls back the whole import.

After successful apply, hot reloads the input manager + rule engine + schedule service so changes take effect immediately.

schema.title: Response Import Config Endpoint V1 Config Import Post

post.description: POST a YAML body — content-type `application/yaml` or `text/yaml`. Returns a plan: what would be created vs updated, plus any errors / warnings. Errors prevent import; warnings don't.

schema.title: Response Validate Config V1 Config Validate Post

post.summary: Validate a YAML config without writing

post.description: External callers (Node-RED, scripts, third-party apps) post here with `type` and `context` (vars used by the template). The service handles routing, throttling, and channel dispatch. Caller does NOT need to know channels, credentials, or templates.

get.description: Returns the overall service status plus a per-component health map. Always returns HTTP 200 — inspect the body to determine status. For a pass/fail probe that fails on essential-component outages, use ``/v1/health/ready`` (returns 503 when not ready).

Returns HTTP 200 when every essential component (database, rule engine, delivery worker) is up, and HTTP 503 when one is down — so an orchestrator or the container healthcheck acts on a dead engine or retry worker instead of a body that always says 200 (F32).
